places.name: Flying Biscuit Café
comments: Unique breakfast options you don't always see.
They serve breakfast until 2pm, which is good. Most other places stop serving by then.
places.blurb: Southern breakfast and brunch café that started in Atlanta, known for fluffy biscuits with cranberry apple butter, moon dusted potatoes, chicken and waffles, and shrimp and grits. The Tiger Town location opened in December 2022 with a dining room and a patio.

places.name: Sushi Kingdom
comments: All you can eat sushi, and it's fresh.
Cool roll options, plus a buffet bar for appetizers.
A robot brings you your sushi when it's done!
Really cool Japanese designs and decorations.
places.blurb: All-you-can-eat sushi and hibachi spot on Pepperell Parkway that opened in summer 2026. Rolls, nigiri and sashimi are made to order and delivered to your table by robot, with a hot bar for appetizers. AYCE tiers are Silver $23.99 (no cold bar), Gold $31.99 (no crab legs) and Diamond $38.99 (full menu) per person.

places.name: Hattie B's Hot Chicken
comments: Not bad, and it's open late downtown.
Not our first choice for chicken.
The pimento mac n cheese is really good.
The chewable ice is good too.
places.blurb: Nashville hot chicken spot that opened in July 2026 in the old Tiger Theatre building on College Street, across from campus near Toomer's Drugs. Chicken comes in heat levels from Southern (no heat) up to Shut the Cluck Up, with Southern sides and a covered patio out front.
places.photoCredit: Hattie B's and The Auburn Villager

places.name: Roni's Mac Bar
comments: On the more expensive side, but unique.
Portions aren't as big as you'd hope.
places.blurb: Build-your-own mac and cheese bar that started in Waco, Texas and blew up on TikTok. The College Street shop opened in June 2025 as the first Roni's in Alabama, serving mac bowls and grilled cheese with your pick of meats, toppings and sauces, and stays open until 2am on football weekends.
places.photoCredit: Roni's Mac Bar and The Auburn Villager

places.name: Guthrie's
comments: They don't do anything that great or that bad.
Open late downtown and always a fun experience. You see people you know.
places.blurb: Chicken finger joint that's been an Auburn staple since 1982, when the Guthrie family brought it down from Haleyville, Alabama. Known for fingers, fries, Texas toast and the signature Guthrie's sauce. This is the downtown location on Glenn Ave, just off Toomer's Corner.

places.name: Chipotle
comments: Like most Chipotles, so you know what you're getting for the most part.
Service is hit or miss, and there can be a huge line sometimes.
Sometimes they're out of an ingredient.
places.blurb: The Chipotle on Magnolia, across from campus at Thomas St. Burritos, bowls, tacos and quesadillas built down the line, open every day until 11pm.

places.name: Firehouse Subs
comments: A little out of the way, but good if you're near the highway.
places.blurb: Hot sub chain started by firefighter brothers in Jacksonville, Florida, known for steamed meats and melted cheese on toasted rolls. This one is on South College near the I-85 interchange.
places.address: 1907 S College St, Suite 108, Auburn, AL 36832

places.name: Toro Sushi
comments: Very fast service. Sometimes it's ready in 1-2 minutes.
Expensive for the amount you get.
Fully customizable poke bowls and sushi.
places.blurb: Campus sushi counter with spots in the Melton Student Center and the Village. Build your own sushi rolls or poke bowls, or grab Asian staples like teriyaki chicken and lo mein.
places.address: Melton Student Center, 255 Heisman Dr, Auburn, AL 36849
places.photoCredit: Sushi Seek and The Auburn Plainsman

places.name: Chick-fil-A
places.blurb: The chicken sandwich chain everyone knows, with locations all over Auburn: W Magnolia by campus, Opelika Rd, E University Dr, the Village and the Student Center. The pin is the W Magnolia drive-thru, open Monday to Saturday and closed Sundays.

places.name: The Edge
comments: All you can eat, with lots and lots of choices.
About $14 to eat without using a swipe.
You're not going here for quality, you're going here for options.
places.blurb: Auburn's main all-you-care-to-eat dining hall at Central Dining, by the Stadium Parking Deck and Parker Hall. It opened in 2021 with eight food stations serving breakfast, lunch and dinner seven days a week. Students use meal plan swipes; everyone else pays at the door.

places.name: Village Dining Hall
comments: Fewer choices than The Edge, but higher quality food.
places.blurb: Tiger Zone, the all-you-care-to-eat dining hall in the Village dining building on the west side of campus. It got a $3.8 million renovation in 2019 with a new kitchen and community-style seating. Meal plan swipes and block meals work here, same as The Edge.

places.name: Einstein Bros. Bagels
comments: On the expensive side for what you get.
places.blurb: Bagel and coffee shop on the ground floor of Haley Center, across from the University Bookstore. Students voted it onto campus in 2016 and it opened in 2017, serving bagels with flavored cream cheeses, breakfast and lunch sandwiches, and espresso drinks.
places.address: Haley Center, 351 W Thach Concourse, Auburn, AL 36849
places.photoCredit: Einstein Bros. Bagels and The Auburn Plainsman

places.name: Tekila
places.blurb: Locally owned Mexican bar and grill on W Magnolia, a couple of blocks from Toomer's Corner. Known for its colorful margaritas, plus street tacos, birria tacos, fajitas and seafood plates like arroz con mariscos.
places.address: 234 W Magnolia Ave, Suite C, Auburn, AL 36832

places.name: Agave Loco
comments: Not as great for larger parties.
places.blurb: Colorful Mexican grill on Opelika Road across from Country's Barbecue, known for big margaritas, sizzling fajitas, burritos and combo plates. There's a sister location in Opelika.

places.name: Acapulco's Mexican Grill
comments: A few times the waiter has taken a long time to get us our checks.
places.blurb: Busy sit-down Mexican spot on South College with a big menu of fajitas, molcajetes, enchiladas, burritos and street tacos, plus a full bar.

places.name: El Dorado
comments: Normal Mexican food, nothing too special.
places.blurb: Longtime Mexican restaurant in a stone building just off South College, and a repeat winner of The Plainsman's Choice for best Mexican food, including 2018 and 2022.
places.photoCredit: Yelp reviewers and The Auburn Plainsman
